summary: Herbert Mills Birdwood studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1851–1854) and Peterhouse (~1854–1858). He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1858 to 1897.

Herbert Niel Randle studied at Hertford College and the University of Oxford (D.Phil.). A scholar of Indology and philosophy, he was Professor of Philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1908–1927) and served as Librarian at the India Office (~1933–1949).

Linguist Herbert Petersson studied at Lund University (Ph.D. 1912) under Nils Olof Mathias Flensburg, as well as at Rostock, Münster, and Copenhagen. He taught at Lund University, becoming ordinary professor of Sanskrit and comparative Indo-European linguistics (1923–1927).

Herbert Pierrepont Houghton, who worked in linguistics and Indology, studied at Amherst, Johns Hopkins (Ph.D. ~1907), and Princeton. He served as President of Waynesburg University (1908–1915) and Professor of Classics at Carleton College (1923–1950).
Philosopher Herbert Schneider studied at the City University of New York and Columbia University. He held an academic post at Columbia University from around 1918 to 1957.
Indologist Herbert Tower Sorley studied at the University of Aberdeen, earning an M.A. around 1914, and received a D.Litt. from the University of Sindh.

Scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Herbert V. Guenther earned degrees at Munich and Vienna. He taught at Vienna and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University before serving as Head of Far Eastern Studies at the University of Saskatchewan (1964–1984).

Herbert W. Duda was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Leipzig (~1928–1932), the University of Breslau (~1936–1944), and the University of Vienna (~1944–1970).

Linguist and historian Herbert Weir Smyth studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen. After posts at Williams, Johns Hopkins, and Bryn Mawr, he served as Eliot Professor of Greek Literature at Harvard University (1902–1925).

Indologist and linguist Herbert William Magoun studied at Grinnell and Johns Hopkins (Ph.D. 1890 under Maurice Bloomfield). He taught at Oberlin and Redfield College, later serving as President of the Massachusetts College of Osteopathy (1921–1926).
Japanologist Herbert Zachert studied under Karl Florenz from around 1927 to 1933. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1941–1945) and the University of Bonn (~1960–1974).

Linguist Herman Almkvist studied at Uppsala University (M.A. 1866), Paris, and Leipzig. He spent his career at Uppsala University, serving as extraordinary professor of comparative linguistics (1878) and full professor of Semitic languages (1892).
Indologist Herman Eildert Buiskool studied under Barend Faddegon at the University of Amsterdam, earning his Ph.D. around 1934. He served as a conservator at Leiden University from 1936 to 1938.
Indologist Herman Frederik Eelsingh studied at Utrecht University from around 1904 to 1908, completing a Ph.D. under the supervision of Willem Caland.

Indologist and linguist Herman Kellgren studied at Helsinki (M.A. 1844) and across Europe under scholars including Franz Bopp, Eugène Burnouf, and Hermann Brockhaus. In 1854, he was appointed Docent of Sanskrit at the University of Helsinki.
Herman Neubronner van der Tuuk was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Groningen (~1840–1845) and Leiden University (~1845–1849).

Linguist Hermann Ammann studied at Freiburg (Ph.D. 1910 under Rudolf Thurneysen) and Heidelberg. After positions at Freiburg, he became ordinary professor of Indo-European and general linguistics at the University of Innsbruck in 1928.

Hermann Beckh worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earning his Ph.D. at Berlin under Richard Pischel. He served as Privatdozent at Berlin (1910–1921) and later taught at the Priesterseminar der Christengemeinschaft Stuttgart (~1922–1937).

Indologist and linguist Hermann Berger earned his Ph.D. at the University of Munich under Helmut Hoffmann. He served as Privatdozent at Munich (1957–1960) and later as Director at Heidelberg University (1964–1993).

Hermann Beythan, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied at the Leipzig Evangelical Lutheran Mission (1895–1901) and under Ramasami Aiyar and Raja Pillai. He was Lecturer in Tamil at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1933–1945).
